headline: Self-employment of 13.8 % stands out, while full-time work sits slightly below the benchmarks.
how_to_read: Flows run from all respondents (left) to employed or not employed (middle) and then to detailed situation (right); width is the share of respondents. Both branch totals are hidden, so branches show as lower bounds (≥) and a hatched "Hidden" flow leaves "Respondents" directly.
key_findings: Full-time work accounts for 72.4 % and self-employment for 13.8 % of respondents.
No respondents are in not seeking work, student, retired or other situations; part-time, other employment and seeking work are hidden.
benchmark: Self-employment is 4.6 pp above Asia (9.2 %) and 5.8 pp above all schools (8.0 %). Full-time work is 2.2 pp below Asia (74.6 %) and 2.5 pp below all schools (74.9 %).
caveats: With n = 29, each person moves the percentages by several points, and both totals are hidden (fewer than 3 people).
